title: Taxonomy - 20 Question Local AI Proof
source_text: Taxonomy identifies, names, and classifies organisms. A named classification group is a taxon. The plural of taxon is taxa. Carl Linnaeus helped establish hierarchical classification and binomial nomenclature. The eight principal ranks, broadest to most specific, are domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. Domain is the broadest main rank. Species is the most specific of these eight ranks. A kingdom contains phyla. A phylum contains classes. A class contains orders. An order contains families. A family contains genera. A genus contains species. Genera is the plural of genus. Family is immediately above genus. Order is immediately above family. The three-domain model recognizes Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya. Animals, plants, and fungi belong to Eukarya. Humans belong to domain Eukarya, kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Mammalia, order Primates, family Hominidae, genus Homo, and species Homo sapiens. Binomial nomenclature uses a genus name followed by a specific epithet. In Homo sapiens, Homo is the genus and sapiens is the specific epithet. The complete species name is Homo sapiens, not sapiens alone. The genus starts with a capital letter. The specific epithet starts with a lowercase letter. Both words are italicized in print. When handwritten, the two words are underlined separately. Scientific names help people communicate across languages and differences in common names. Phylogeny describes evolutionary history and relationships. Systematics studies biological diversity and evolutionary relationships. New evidence can lead scientists to revise classifications. Scientists compare DNA sequences, anatomy, molecular characteristics, and fossils to investigate relationships. Similar appearance alone does not prove a close evolutionary relationship. A phylogenetic tree represents a hypothesis about evolutionary relationships. A rooted tree identifies an ancestral lineage for all organisms shown. An unrooted tree shows relationships without identifying a root. A branch point represents a common ancestor where lineages diverge. Sister taxa share an immediate common ancestor. A polytomy has more than two descendant lineages from a branch point and often represents an unresolved branching order. Rotating branches around a node does not alter their relationships. The left-to-right order of tips alone does not establish relatedness. Scientists compare how recently groups shared a common ancestor. Branch length indicates time or amount of change only when the diagram provides an appropriate scale. A living species at a tip is not automatically the ancestor of another living species at a tip.
